chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyri narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is written that one who consumes the wealth of orphans unjustly, the consequence of that will overtake him in his wake after him in this world.

For indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring, would fear on their account, so let them be careful of (their duty to) Allah, and let them speak right words.'
And as for the Hereafter, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says:
(As for) those who swallow the property of the orphans unjustly, surely they only swallow fire into their bellies and they shall enter burning fire.

key_terms.آکِلَ مَالِ الْیَتَامَی: One who consumes/eats the wealth of orphans
key_terms.یَأْکُلُونَ فِی بُطُونِهِمْ ناراً: They swallow fire into their bellies

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for consuming an orphan's wealth unjustly according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from the book of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) that usurping an orphan's wealth unjustly brings calamity in this world and severe punishment in the Hereafter. The text cites Quranic verses from Surah An-Nisa to illustrate the worldly consequence (fear for weak offspring) and the afterlife consequence (swallowing fire). This tradition highlights the concept of *'aqibah* (consequence) extending to one's descendants, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding financial sins.
